title: Rethinking Prediction Horizons: Decoupling Model Queries from State Updates in Few-Step MeanFlow
abstract: arXiv:2610.20071v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: MeanFlow predicts interval-average velocities, but conventional few-step sampling ties the interval queried from the model to the duration of the state update. We separate these two quantities at inference, fixing the model, update grid, and number of queries while varying the prediction horizon. Our central finding is that the horizon response depends on both query position and the states entering that query. Across seven independently trained CIFAR-10 checkpoints at classifier-free guidance (CFG) scale 2, a longer horizon worsens FID at early steps but improves it at the midpoint. To probe whether query time alone determines this response, we fix the midpoint query and current/subsequent guidance while changing only earlier CFG. In held-out factorial outcomes on five previously studied checkpoints, the mean midpoint horizon benefit increases from 0.109 to 1.308 FID, indicating sensitivity to the incoming-state distribution. translated_title: 重新思考预测视野：在少步MeanFlow中解耦模型查询与状态更新
translated_abstract: MeanFlow预测区间平均速度，但传统的少步采样将模型查询的区间与状态更新的持续时间绑定在一起。我们在推理阶段将这两个量分离，在固定模型、更新网格和查询次数的同时改变预测视野。我们的核心发现是：视野的响应同时取决于查询位置以及进入该查询的状态。在七个独立训练的CIFAR-10检查点（分类器自由引导CFG尺度为2）上，较长的视野在早期步骤会恶化FID，但在中点处会改善FID。为了探究是否仅查询时间决定了这一响应，我们固定中点查询以及当前/后续引导，仅改变较早的CFG。在五个先前研究过的检查点上的保留因子实验结果中，中点视野的平均收益从0.109 FID增加到1.308 FID，表明其对输入状态分布具有敏感性。一个冻结的……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文在少步MeanFlow采样中解耦了模型查询区间与状态更新时长，发现预测视野对生成质量的影响并非仅由查询时间决定，还依赖于进入查询的状态分布——中点视野收益随早期引导设置的变化可从0.109显著增大至1.308 FID。
en_tdlr: Decoupling model query intervals from state update durations in few-step MeanFlow reveals that prediction horizon effects on FID depend on both query position and the incoming state distribution, with midpoint horizon benefits increasing from 0.109 to 1.308 FID as earlier guidance changes.
